cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-119 requires operations that read/write outside intended memory boundaries. The demonstrated behavior is reading a potentially large amount of data into memory, not buffer overflow/underflow. The ASN.1 decoder may have internal bounds checking.

connection.evidence: CONTENT_LENGTH HTTP header (attacker-controlled) is converted to integer length, which directly controls the amount of data read from wsgi.input stream and passed to codec.decode.

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the primary mechanism that reads request body data. If reverted, no request body would be read, preventing any memory allocation from this source.

security_control.evidence: No bounds checking on CONTENT_LENGTH before using it to allocate memory via read().
security_control.required_control: Bounds validation on attacker-controlled size parameter before memory allocation
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-119 requires preventing operations that exceed allocated buffer boundaries. For memory allocation based on untrusted size, validation is required.
existing_controls_checked: ASN.1 decoder internal validation (unknown), WSGI server limits (unknown)
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No validation of CONTENT_LENGTH value before using it in read(). Negative values may cause undefined behavior. Large positive values could cause excessive memory allocation.

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential memory exhaustion or DoS from large allocations, but not demonstrated buffer overflow/underflow. The exact impact depends on ASN.1 decoder implementation and WSGI server limits.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, no request body would be read from wsgi.input, preventing any memory allocation based on CONTENT_LENGTH and eliminating the potential for memory exhaustion from this source.
supporting_evidence: CONTENT_LENGTH HTTP header is attacker-controlled and converted to integer without validation
The length parameter directly controls how much data is read from wsgi.input stream
The read data is passed to ASN.1 decoder which may allocate memory proportional to input size
contradicting_evidence: CWE-119 specifically addresses buffer overflow/underflow operations, not memory exhaustion from large allocations
The code reads data into Python objects, not raw memory buffers with fixed boundaries
No evidence of out-of-bounds memory operations in the demonstrated code path
unresolved_facts: Maximum request size limit imposed by WSGI server configuration
Behavior of env["wsgi.input"].read() with negative or zero length values
Internal bounds checking in codec.decode ASN.1 parser
Whether Python's memory management prevents traditional buffer overflows
